project.name: SpikeWatch
project.purpose: PyQt5 desktop app for monitoring price spikes on Binance & Bitget USDT perpetual futures, opening simulated (paper) trades on spikes with configurable TP/SL/trailing-SL, and backtesting pluggable strategies against historical klines.

tech_stack.http_client: aiohttp (live + backtest); requests (only two sync startup calls)
tech_stack.concurrency: Single background daemon thread hosting one asyncio event loop; cooperative cancellation via asyncio.Event
tech_stack.persistence: SQLite (WAL mode) with CSV mirror for rollback compatibility
tech_stack.testing: pytest; 9 test files; no real network (FakeSession mocks aiohttp)

architecture_pattern.style: Layered: UI (PyQt) ⇄ Qt signal bus ⇄ Engine (single asyncio loop) ⇄ Data layer (async REST + rate limiter + SQLite store) + pure-function strategies & trade-state machine

decisions.title: Single asyncio loop on one background thread
decisions.rationale: Replaces the legacy 3-thread / 3-asyncio.run / blocking-requests model. One thread is enough for our throughput; cooperative cancellation via asyncio.Event is simpler than threading.Event coordination.
decisions.evidence: src/core/engine.py:_ensure_loop; live monitors + backtester run as tasks on the same loop

decisions.title: Pure trade-state machine shared by live + backtest
decisions.rationale: Live update_trade_pnl and all backtest simulators run through the same step(trade, bar, params) function. Live/backtest divergence is now structurally impossible.
decisions.evidence: src/core/trade_state.py; tests/test_trade_state.py (15 golden tests); tests/test_strategies.py (registry path == legacy shim, byte-identical)

decisions.title: Pluggable Strategy registry
decisions.rationale: Strategy ABC with self-registering subclasses. Adding a strategy = one new file in strategies_pkg/, zero edits to engine or UI.

decisions.title: SQLite-backed lifetime trade history with CSV mirror
decisions.rationale: WAL mode for safe concurrent reads. Idempotent on (symbol, exchange, open_time) so a retried close cannot double-count. CSV mirror preserved so rolling back to <0.2.0 doesn't lose data.

decisions.title: Header-driven rate limiter, not a fixed throttle
decisions.rationale: Both exchanges publish remaining budget in response headers. Reading them lets us slow down BEFORE we get 429s. Far cheaper than recovering from an IP ban.
decisions.evidence: src/data/rate_limit.py; module-level LIMITERS keyed by exchange

decisions.title: Open-trade state typed; closed-trade records stay dicts
decisions.rationale: Open trades are read frequently by the engine — attribute access on a Trade dataclass means typos fail at edit time. Closed trades are the persistence boundary (SQLite rows, CSV mirror, Qt signal payloads); keeping them as dicts means the wire format is stable.
decisions.evidence: engine.binance_open_trades: dict[str, Trade]; close_trade writes dict to trade_store

decisions.title: Crypto 24/7/365 calendar for metric annualisation
decisions.rationale: The legacy code used 252 trading days (equity markets). Crypto never closes; using 365 (or 24*365, etc.) is honest. One Sharpe method, one resampled equity curve.

decisions.title: Versioning via single __version__ + CHANGELOG-gated bumps
decisions.rationale: src/__init__.py.__version__ is the only place the number lives. test_version.py fails if you bump without writing a matching CHANGELOG section, so the bump is always intentional and documented.

components.role: Trading engine — orchestrates live monitoring, trade management, backtest execution
responsibilities: Lazily start one background daemon thread with one asyncio loop
Live monitors run as cooperative asyncio tasks (NOT separate threads)
Each monitor owns one aiohttp.ClientSession (TCP/TLS reuse across cycles)
Per-cycle: fan out fetch_prices_batch with Semaphore(20); on signal -> open_trade; on every result -> update_trade_pnl through trade_state.step
Emit sweep_telemetry_signal per cycle for the status bar
Backtest runs as a third task on the same loop; pagination delegated to data.exchange_api
Holds open trades as dict[str, Trade] (dataclass); closed trades persisted via trade_store

components.role: Qt signal bus connecting engine -> UI
Pure TP/SL/trailing-SL state machine — single source of truth shared by live engine and backtest simulators
responsibilities: Trade @dataclass: symbol, direction, prices, trailing state
Bar @dataclass with from_candle / from_tick constructors
StepParams: tp_pct, sl_pct, trailing_sl_pct, activation_pct
step(trade, bar, params) -> StepResult: applies one observation, returns updated trade + maybe closure
open_trade(...) creates Trade with TP/SL derived from StepParams
force_close(trade, price, reason) for manual / end-of-backtest closures
pinned_invariants: TP wins over SL within one candle
Trailing SL ratchets only in the favourable direction
Activation can fire the new trailing SL on the SAME bar (legacy convention)

responsibilities: Strategy ABC with NAME, PARAMS (list[ParamSpec]), signal(i, bars), exit_signal(...)
ParamSpec: name, label, default, kind (int/float/str), help text
@register decorator + STRATEGIES global dict
run_backtest(name, raw_params, symbol, klines, ...) drives the unified state machine

components.role: Built-in strategies, one per file (auto-registered on import)
Backwards-compat shim — simulate_*_trades(...) delegates to run_backtest
components.notes: Kept so any external callers of v0.1.0 still work. Tests pin byte-identical output vs the registry path.

responsibilities: calculate_equity_curve(klines, trades, initial_capital) -> (times, values)
calculate_advanced_metrics(...) -> MetricsResult (Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, max DD, profit factor, win rate, annualised return)
Single Sharpe method: log returns of resampled equity curve, annualized with crypto 24/7/365 calendar
Auto-picks periodicity from median sample interval

components.role: Async REST clients for Binance + Bitget public market data
responsibilities: fetch_klines(session, exchange, ...) — normalises Bitget's newest-first string payloads to Binance's ascending numeric shape
fetch_prices_batch(...) — fans out a batch with Semaphore(20); records every response to the rate limiter; awaits limiter.pause_if_needed before/after
paginate_historical_klines — Binance forward (startTime), Bitget backward (endTime); returns chronological list
Single source of truth for BITGET_TIMEFRAME_MAP
Sync startup helpers (get_*_symbols_sync) kept for the UI's blocking startup path
LimitConfig per exchange (header name, budget, window, soft/hard thresholds)
RateLimiter.record_response(headers, status_code) — Binance 'used so far' direct; Bitget 'remaining' inverted
RateLimiter.pause_if_needed() — short pause at >=80%, full-window pause at >=95%
Exponential 429 backoff (2^streak, capped 30s); reset on next 2xx
Module-level LIMITERS dict so one limiter is shared per exchange across the session

components.role: SQLite-backed trade history with CSV mirror
responsibilities: Schema: id, symbol, direction, exchange, open_time, close_time, open_price, close_price, pnl_percent, close_reason; UNIQUE(symbol, exchange, open_time)
WAL journal mode; one connection per thread via threading.local
record_close(trade) — idempotent on the UNIQUE key
recent(limit) / filtered(symbol/exchange/close_reason/since/until/order/limit) / count()
ORDER BY whitelist defends against injection
import_csv() one-shot migration from legacy demo_trade_results.csv
dual_write_csv=True mirrors every insert (rollback safety)

data_flows.name: Live spike monitoring & paper-trade execution
data_flows.trigger: User clicks Start Monitoring with threshold/timeframe/TP/SL/trailing-SL
steps: engine._ensure_loop() lazily spins up the background asyncio thread
Two _monitor(exchange, ...) tasks scheduled on the loop
Each task opens one aiohttp.ClientSession reused across cycles
Per cycle: fetch_prices_batch fans out with Semaphore(20); rate_limit.pause_if_needed wraps the batch
For each symbol w/ data: if currently open -> update_trade_pnl through trade_state.step; if pct >= threshold -> open_trade
Closures go through close_trade -> trade_store.record_close (SQLite + CSV mirror)
Per cycle: sweep_telemetry_signal emitted with {exchange, cycle, symbols_ok, symbols_seen, elapsed_s}
UI slots run on the Qt main thread; status bar reflects telemetry colour-coded
data_flows.data_out: trades table rows + UI list updates + status bar

data_flows.name: Historical backtest of a registered strategy
data_flows.trigger: User picks symbol/exchange/strategy/date-range and clicks Run Backtest
steps: engine.run_backtest schedules _execute_backtest on the same asyncio loop
paginate_historical_klines streams pages from the exchange (Binance forward, Bitget backward)
strategy_base.run_backtest(name, params, ...) walks bars; signal() opens trades; trade_state.step handles TP/SL/trailing; exit_signal() handles strategy-driven exits
core.utils.calculate_equity_curve compounds PnL across the kline timeline
backtest_finished_signal((klines, results, symbol, exchange, equity)) emitted
UI computes MetricsResult, logs Sharpe / Sortino / Calmar / drawdown / profit factor / annualised return
Price Chart + Equity Chart buttons enabled

data_flows.name: Lifetime trade history available immediately on launch
steps: TradeStore.__init__: opens SQLite (creates schema if missing), then runs import_csv() to absorb any legacy demo_trade_results.csv rows

concurrency_model.description: One background daemon thread runs one asyncio event loop. Was: three daemon threads each calling asyncio.run() with blocking requests.

threads.name: Qt main
threads.duty: UI events, slot execution, widget updates

threads.name: SpikeWatch-asyncio
threads.duty: Hosts the single asyncio loop running monitor + backtest tasks

synchronization: asyncio.Event (stop_event) signalled from Qt via loop.call_soon_threadsafe
asyncio.Semaphore(20) caps in-flight fetches per exchange
RateLimiter (per exchange) gates additional requests via pause_if_needed
TradeStore: one sqlite3 connection per thread via threading.local; WAL journal mode supports concurrent reads

tests.covers: Pure step() machine: TP/SL precedence, trailing activation, ratchet, force_close, live-tick mode
Each built-in simulator end-to-end on synthetic klines
Registry, ParamSpec casts, legacy-shim byte-identical equivalence, user-defined Strategy
Async client behaviour against a FakeSession: Binance/Bitget normalisation, batch pct/current, pagination
Header parsing, soft/hard thresholds, 429 backoff + reset, rolling window
Round-trip, idempotency, filters, ORDER BY whitelist, CSV mirror, legacy import
Equity curve compounding, hand-computed drawdown, Sharpe/Sortino/Calmar properties, crypto calendar
Engine open-trades hold Trade dataclass; open/update/close round-trip (PyQt5 only)
SignalEmitter declares expected signals; telemetry payload shape (PyQt5 only)
SemVer format + CHANGELOG entry exists for current version

constraints: PyQt5 only — bumping to PyQt6 will need signal/slot syntax + QDate API updates.
Public endpoints only. The product is a paper-trading simulator; no authenticated order endpoints without a secrets layer + explicit user confirmation.
trade_state behaviours pinned by tests/test_trade_state.py — TP-vs-SL precedence and trailing ratchet are intentional and shared across live + backtest.
trade_store schema is UNIQUE on (symbol, exchange, open_time). Any future re-entry on the same minute will be silently deduped.
BITGET_TIMEFRAME_MAP is the single source of truth — adding a timeframe means adding to that one constant.
test_version.py forces a CHANGELOG entry for any version bump.
removed_in_0_2_0: Engine's _init_trade_history_file + inline csv writes (TradeStore owns the file)
Duplicated Bitget timeframe map (was in engine + exchange_api)
Inline backtest pagination in engine.execute_backtest (now in data.exchange_api.paginate_historical_klines)
Three independent simulate_*_trades implementations (collapsed to one driver + 3 strategy classes)

outstanding_followups.title: ExchangeClient Protocol full subclasses
outstanding_followups.note: Data layer is exchange-agnostic at call sites now, but a full Protocol-and-subclass split was deferred. Worth doing when a third exchange arrives.

outstanding_followups.title: Async startup symbol fetch
outstanding_followups.note: Still uses the sync requests-based path, which briefly blocks the UI thread on launch. A splash screen or one-shot asyncio.to_thread would smooth this out.

outstanding_followups.title: DB schema migrations
outstanding_followups.note: Today's CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is fine for additive changes (new column with default) but doesn't handle removed/renamed columns. Add a versions table + applied migrations list before the first column drop.

good_starting_points_for_changes: Add a strategy: write src/core/strategies_pkg/<name>.py with a Strategy subclass + @register; import it from strategies_pkg/__init__.py. Zero edits to engine or UI.
Add a column to the trade history: ALTER TABLE in TradeStore._SCHEMA (additive only), update record_close + _row_to_dict, document in CHANGELOG, bump MINOR.
Add a metric: extend MetricsResult and calculate_advanced_metrics; add a golden test in tests/test_metrics.py; surface in main_window._handle_backtest_completion.
do_not_touch_without_care: trade_state.step's TP-before-SL precedence — every simulator and the live engine rely on it; changing it invalidates all historical backtests.
TradeStore's UNIQUE(symbol, exchange, open_time) — relied on for idempotency.
paginate_historical_klines direction asymmetry (Binance forward, Bitget backward) — the reassembly logic is order-sensitive.
SignalEmitter signatures — UI slots depend on argument shapes; test_signals.py pins them.
agent_hints.where_versioning_lives: src/__init__.py.__version__ is the single source of truth; CHANGELOG.md must have a matching ## [x.y.z] entry or test_version.py fails.
